newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France sets final merger terms for group.
newsitem.headline: Air France sets final merger terms for group.

text.p: An announced merger between international airline Air France and regional and European carrier Air France Europe will be done on the basis of 32 Air France shares for one Air France Europe share, Air France said on Wednesday.
The parity, which values Air France seven times that of Air France Europe, was first announced on a preliminary basis on June 27.

Seventy seven Air France shares will be offered in exchange for 80 shares in Groupe Air France SA, the holding company whose assets are almost exclusively made up of shares in Air France and Air France Europe, Air France said in a statement.
The parities were based on studies done by Lazard Freres & Cie for Air France and Societe Generale for Air France Europe, using discounted cash flow and revalued net asset bases.

The boards of Air France and Air France Europe adopted the terms at meetings on July 30, and a July 29 meeting for Groupe Air France. The parities, as well a name change to Groupe Air France, will be put to shareholders meetings on September 12.

After the share exchanges and cancellation of Air France's holdings of its own shares following the merger with Groupe Air France, Air France's issued capital will rise to 10.55 billion francs ($1.7 billion) from 9.20 billion. The merger premium will total 767 million francs. The state will hold a direct holding of 94.57 percent.

The merger opens up "a new dynamic for clients, employees and the group's shareholders, by the integration, as in the principal European companies, of complementary domestic and international activities into a single entity..." Air France said.
